candidate_sentence_map.S1: Tallinna Sadam Group reported a year of resilient financial performance in 2025, characterized by stable revenue and significant improvements in profitability and operational efficiency.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Consolidated revenue amounted to EUR 118.7 million, representing a slight decline of 0.8% compared to the previous year.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: This minor decrease was primarily driven by a sharp reduction in charter fees from the icebreaker Botnica, which fell by 34% to EUR 7.9 million due to a lower utilization rate of 49%.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: However, this negative impact was more than offset by growth in the core port operations.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Revenue from vessel dues increased by 8% to EUR 34.1 million, supported by calls from larger tankers and cruise ships.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Passenger fees grew by 3% to EUR 12.2 million, while cargo charges rose by 3% to EUR 6.9 million, reflecting increased handling volumes.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Lease income also expanded by 3% to EUR 14.6 million due to fee indexing.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Operational metrics demonstrated a strong recovery in cargo and passenger flows.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Cargo volume grew by 5.1% to 13.8 million tonnes, with liquid bulk seeing a substantial 47% increase, partly recovering from previous sanction-related declines.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: The number of passengers reached 8.3 million, a 1.0% increase, bolstered by a 25% surge in cruise passengers and a 10% rise in cruise ship calls.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Ferry services maintained steady performance, serving 2.5 million passengers and 1.2 million vehicles across domestic routes, despite a slight 0.6% decrease in the number of voyages.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: The Group’s ability to manage costs effectively led to marked improvements in profitability.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Operating expenses decreased by 10% to EUR 36.4 million, largely due to lower technical maintenance and repair costs for the icebreaker Botnica, which had been elevated in the prior year due to a technical failure.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Consequently, operating profit rose by 12.2% to EUR 32.7 million, and the operating profit margin improved from 24.4% to 27.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Adjusted EBITDA increased by 6.4% to EUR 56.5 million, with the adjusted EBITDA margin expanding to 47.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Net profit grew by 17.3% to EUR 22.5 million, although this growth was partially tempered by a higher dividend income tax expense resulting from a change in Estonian tax regulations.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Financial position remained robust, with equity increasing by 0.9% to EUR 380.9 million and net debt decreasing by 15.5% to EUR 141.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The Group maintained a strong liquidity position, with cash and cash equivalents rising to EUR 32.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: Capital investments totaled EUR 33.2 million, a 14.4% decrease from the previous year, focusing on infrastructure upgrades at Paldiski South Harbour and Muuga Harbour, as well as ferry maintenance.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: The company continued its shareholder-friendly policy, distributing a dividend of EUR 19.2 million, which represented 100% of the prior year’s profit.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: Overall, the period was defined by successful cost management, operational recovery in core port activities, and strengthened financial metrics.

evaluation.label: Generally yes
evaluation.justification: K1, K2, K3, K4, K5, and K7 are PRESENT with clear coverage in the candidate summary. K6 and K8 are MISSING entirely—no mention of war impacts or environmental sustainability metrics. The summary captures most core financial and operational themes, but the absence of two HIGH/MEDIUM criteria (war impact and sustainability) prevents a perfect score. The overall picture is strong but incomplete.
